follow-up time: From enrollment during pregnancy until after vaginal delivery
cohort: 57 pregnant women (17 with ulcerative colitis, 23 with Crohn's disease, and 17 healthy controls)
finding: The incidence of postpartum anal incontinence was comparable between women with inflammatory bowel disease and healthy controls.
mod_finding: The incidence of postpartum anal incontinence was not significantly different between women with inflammatory bowel disease and healthy controls, and cesarean section was not found to be indicated for these patients.
